html:
The Náayeri, known in Spanish as the Cora, are an Indigenous people of the Sierra del Nayar in the state of Nayarit, western Mexico. They speak a Uto-Aztecan language related to that of their neighbours, the Wixárika (Huichol).

Their rugged mountains kept them free long after the rest of the region fell to Spain. Only in 1722 did Spanish troops take their stronghold, the Mesa del Nayar, and open the sierra to Jesuit missions. Cora religion today blends old and Catholic beliefs, seen above all in their Holy Week festival. The coastal Totorames lived to their west, and the territory lay on the edge of New Spain.
